novel_features.name: Live Trading Pulse
novel_features.description: Instant overview of today's trading session: wins, losses, running PnL, regime, and setup distribution.
novel_features.rationale: Requires join across trading_sessions + postmortems + calibration for today's date — no single API call covers this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when you need a pre-market or mid-session status check without opening a dashboard.

novel_features.name: Trading Calibration Summary
novel_features.description: Current win rate by setup type and market regime from calibration history + recent sessions.
novel_features.rationale: Requires aggregating trading_calibration rows by setup + regime and joining recent session outcomes.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before sizing a trade to confirm calibration data supports the setup in the current regime.

novel_features.name: Trading Setup Drift Alert
novel_features.description: Detects when your premortem setup distribution is drifting toward lower expected-value setups before P&L shows it.
novel_features.rationale: Rolling window aggregation over premortems joined to calibration.expected_value per setup — no single query or dashboard catches this early.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use weekly to catch unconscious setup drift before it becomes a drawdown.

novel_features.name: MCP Reliability Report
novel_features.description: Latency percentiles and error rates per MCP server, with auth error overlay.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local join across mcp_activity_logs + mcp_auth_errors + mcp_servers — three tables with no FK relationship.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when diagnosing agent failures that may be caused by a degraded MCP backend.

novel_features.name: MCP Blast Radius
novel_features.description: Shows which NatureOS tasks failed downstream of MCP auth errors within a time window.
novel_features.rationale: Temporal anti-join across mcp_auth_errors + mcp_activity_logs + natureos_task_queue with no FK — only possible via local time-window correlation.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when agents are failing and you need to trace whether an MCP auth error is the root cause.

novel_features.name: Memory Load by Agent
novel_features.description: Which agents have the most active memories, ranked by importance, with expiry alerts.
novel_features.rationale: Requires aggregation across active_memory by agent_id with importance weighting — not a single endpoint.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an agent is behaving oddly to check if it is over- or under-loaded with context.

novel_features.name: Brain Activity Window
novel_features.description: All thoughts, agent messages, and shared_state changes in a time window — cross-domain activity snapshot.
novel_features.rationale: Time-windowed join across three tables with no FK. The only way to see what the system did in the last N hours.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use at start of day to catch up on what agents did overnight.

novel_features.name: Thought-to-Task Latency
novel_features.description: How long insights sit in thoughts before becoming NatureOS agent tasks, by topic.
novel_features.rationale: Fuzzy-joins thoughts.topics to natureos_dual_model_tasks.project_slug on creation timestamps — requires local cross-table text matching.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to identify which thought topics are being ignored by the agent system.

novel_features.name: Agent Deadlock Detection
novel_features.description: Finds agents holding shared_state locks while sending no messages — potential deadlock.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-references shared_state.locked_by against agent_messages.sender recency via time-window anti-join. No FK exists.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when agents seem stuck but no error is surfaced — often a silent lock.

novel_features.name: Agent Throughput
novel_features.description: NatureOS task completion rates by agent type over a rolling window, with backlog depth.
novel_features.rationale: Requires aggregation of natureos_task_queue completions by agent_type + time window — not a single endpoint.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for daily agent health check to see if any agent type is falling behind.

novel_features.name: Cross-Domain Anomaly Detection
novel_features.description: Detects unusual spikes: MCP auth error floods, memory expiry cliffs, task queue backlogs — all at once.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-domain pattern detection across 4+ tables with time-window comparison. No dashboard covers all domains simultaneously.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when something feels off but you are not sure where — surfaces the domain with the highest deviation.

novel_features.name: Skill Gap Analysis
novel_features.description: Which skill domains have low proficiency relative to tool usage frequency.
novel_features.rationale: Joins skills.proficiency + tool_usage_stats.tool to compare declared capability vs. actual system usage.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use monthly to identify which capability areas need reinforcement based on actual workload.

narrative.headline: Your AI infrastructure CLI: offline analytics across trading, memory, agents, and MCP — all from one binary.
narrative.value_prop: brainos-pp-cli syncs your Supabase backend to a local SQLite store, enabling sub-second cross-domain queries that no single API call or dashboard can answer. Trading drift alerts, MCP blast radius traces, agent deadlock detection, and thought-to-task latency — all offline, all composable with jq.

quickstart.comment: mirror all key tables to local SQLite
what happened in the last 2 hours

troubleshoots.fix: brainos-pp-cli sync --full --table thoughts to force full resync

narrative.when_to_use: Use brainos-pp-cli when you need to query your AI infrastructure backend without opening a dashboard. Best for morning standups (trading pulse, brain since), incident response (mcp blast-radius, agents deadlock), and weekly reviews (trading drift, skills gap). It is the only tool that joins trading, memory, MCP, and agent data in a single offline query.
